_what_this_is: The reader-facing copy for the Krites read: the natural-language QUESTION each prepared run answers, and the FRAME — the section leads and transitions that re-voice the four-part read as an answer to that question. Written by Logothetes (Aerine's cast owner) under D-39 items 2 and 4, job 054a910a. Rigging renders; nothing here is generated.
_why_the_question_is_data_and_not_markup: 'What this run was asked' currently shows the seed chips. The seeds are the PARSE, not the prompt — a person asks a question, and the seeds are what it resolved to. So the question is content with its own owner (this office) and the chips stay derived from the fixture. Putting the question in the page's HTML would put copy behind a build step and give it no owner; putting it here keeps one source of truth for it and lets the parse be checked.
_the_check_a_build_must_run: For every run, questions[run].parses_to MUST equal fixtures/free-run-<run>.json _fixture.params, in order. That equality is the whole claim the surface makes when it prints the question above the chips — if it ever fails, the page is showing a question that is not what was asked. Fail the build; do not reconcile by editing parses_to. Verified equal for all five runs on 2026-09-22.
_barred_substrings: Every reader-facing string in this file — the questions and the frame, i.e. every key not beginning with an underscore — was checked against engine/krites-emitted-fields.json _barred_substrings and is clean. The check caught one hit on the first pass and it was rewritten, which is the only evidence that the check is real. It is scoped to reader-facing copy on the engine file's own precedent: that file applies its list to `paths`, while its own underscore-prefixed notes contain barred words in the course of naming them. Applied to prose the list is a flag, not the control: the controls are rider 1 and THESMO-PROP-2026-09-20-002. Applied to prose literally it would bar the page's existing disclaimer, which exists to say the page does not do the barred thing. Reasoning in the delivery document, section 4.5.
_grammar: The invitation (frame.part_five) is bound by THESMO-PROP-2026-09-20-002, which is PROPOSED and not ratified. Sentences written to that proposal as it stands are marked in the delivery document, with the one sentence the grammar refuses and the replacement that survives it. Nothing here may be treated as grammar-cleared before the founder ratifies.

consumer-ibsd.question: Sometimes when I eat, I'll suddenly have to go poop an hour later — often runny. What causes that?
consumer-ibsd._note: The founder's own words, verbatim and unedited (D-39). 'Suddenly have to go' after eating is the urgency-and-looseness pattern that parses to ibs_d; 'often runny' is diarrhea; 'an hour later' is transit_time. It is kept exactly as he wrote it because it is the model for the register, and an edit of the model teaches the wrong register to every question after it.

consumer-fibre.question: I've been eating more whole grains and beans and now I'm bloated most afternoons. People keep telling me it's FODMAPs and not the fiber itself. Which one is it?
consumer-fibre._note: US spelling — fiber, per D-39 item 3. The word FODMAP is in the reader's mouth rather than ours because this reader arrives having already been told it by somebody; a question that parses to fodmap without ever containing it would make the chip look like our inference about them rather than their own words.

device-gas.question: If an instrument could read hydrogen, methane, hydrogen sulfide and the other volatile compounds in a breath sample, which of those does the research actually tie to gut symptoms, and how well is each one evidenced?
device-gas._note: Conditional on purpose. Rider 4 bars citing, implying or projecting device readings, and no Aeriscope datum exists — so this run's asker cannot be an instrument reporting numbers. The asker is whoever is choosing which gases an instrument would read, and the question is a canon question. The run's internal label names Aeriscope; this reader-facing line does not, and must not.

agent-relay.question: Relaying for my principal: constipation-predominant IBS, and methane keeps coming up in what they're reading. Return what canon holds across the desks on that combination, with the grade on each claim, and name what canon does not hold.
agent-relay._note: Written as an agent writes: it declares whose context it carries, states the context rather than performing it, and asks for the two things a person would not think to ask for — the grade on every claim and the named absences. That last clause is why an agent is a good customer for this read and a good test of it.

unresolved-params.question: I'm perimenopausal, I've been gluten-free for years, and I keep reading about the gut mucus layer — mucin. Do those three connect to each other?
unresolved-params._note: The honest-failure run, so the question honestly contains what canon does not hold: mucin locates claims, gluten_free and perimenopause locate nothing at all. The reader is not told they asked badly. They are told canon has not been there — which is the one run on this page where the product's actual claim is visible.

frame._what_this_is: The four-part read, re-voiced as an answer to the question above it. The movement is the founder's: where canon is dense and what it says -> where it thins -> what is one hop from there and what those links point to -> the invitation. Part three and part four are ONE move, not two; part five is new. See the delivery document, section 4.1.

part_one.heading: What we know
part_one.lead: Here is where canon lands on that question, desk by desk, with the grade the literature gave each claim. Where several desks land on the same ground, that is coverage — more of what is known is in view. It is not extra evidence: every claim keeps its own grade, and canon does not get stronger because two desks happened to land on it.
part_one.transition_out: That is the dense part of the question. Now the thin part.

part_two.heading: Where it thins
part_two.lead: Thin here means thinly connected, not disputed. These are the desks the question reached least — and where a desk came back with nothing, the reason is named, every time. A desk showing nothing is never the same as a desk with nothing in it.
part_two.transition_out: A thin desk is not an empty desk. Here is what canon holds there anyway, and the link that reached it.

part_three.eyebrow: Part three — half the read, not a footnote
part_three.heading: What we know there anyway
part_three.lead: These are the claims canon holds in the desks the question was thinnest in. This is the part of the answer you did not already have.
part_three.transition_out: Each one was reached from something in the question, in a single hop. Those hops are printed next, so you can judge them.

part_four.heading: Worth a look
part_four.lead: Each link shows what the two claims share and the grade at each end. A link the literature itself asserts is marked as such. A link we put together is ours, not the literature's, and it carries no grade of its own — joining two graded claims does not produce a third graded claim. These are reading routes. Nothing on this page tells you to do, take or change anything.
part_four.transition_out: Where a link runs out, that is the edge of what canon has been asked about this question.

part_five.heading: What canon does not hold yet
part_five.lead: Every absence named above is an open assignment, not a dead end. Aerine's collectors work from exactly this list: a desk with nothing connected to a question like this one is a gap someone goes and fills, and the next reader who asks it gets the answer this run could not give.
part_five.nearest_held_label: What canon already holds nearest to it
part_five.nearest_held_lead: For each gap, the closest thing canon does hold — the claim a new paper would be read against if one came in.
part_five.capability_line: Aerine reads what you bring her: breath-gas series, stool composition panels, food logs, papers. That list is the same for every reader and does not change with what a run returned. She reads what arrives; she does not send anyone out to fetch anything.
part_five.closing: None of this is a thing to do. It is a list of what the literature has not been asked yet.
